title: Definition of Partnership
en: A Partnership is a business relationship in which two or more competent persons agree to carry on a lawful business together with the objective of earning profit and sharing that profit (or loss) according to an agreed arrangement. The agreement may be written or oral depending upon the laws applicable in a country.

title: Simple Explanation
en: Imagine two friends. One knows cooking. One has money. Instead of opening two separate restaurants, they decide to open one restaurant together. They both invest. They both work. They both share profit. This is called Partnership.

title: Story Based Learning: Riya & Arjun's Bakery

problem.en: Riya and Arjun studied together in college. After graduation they wanted to start a bakery. Riya invested ₹8,00,000. Arjun invested ₹12,00,000. Riya managed production. Arjun managed marketing.

steps.text: After one year they earned a profit of ₹6,00,000.
According to their agreement, they shared profit equally.
This is one example of Partnership.

final_answer: Why is an agreement needed? If they hadn't decided who invests, manages, or gets a salary, arguments would begin. This is why a Partnership Deed is important.

title: Universal Concept
en: Partnership exists in almost every country. Although laws differ, the idea remains the same. People combine Money, Skills, Experience, Time, and Resources to achieve a common business objective.

title: Why Should I Learn This?
en: Suppose someday you Open a tuition class, Start a software company, Open a medical clinic, Start a YouTube channel, Launch a startup, or Open a restaurant. If another person joins you, you are entering a Partnership. This chapter prepares you for real life.

title: Key Features
en:
1. Agreement: No Partnership exists without an agreement.
2. Two or More Persons: One person cannot form Partnership.
3. Lawful Business: Illegal businesses cannot create valid partnerships.
4. Profit Motive: The objective must be earning profit. Charity is not Partnership.
5. Mutual Agency: Every partner acts as Owner and Agent. This is the heart of Partnership.

title: The Most Important Concept: Mutual Agency
en: This is the concept students fear. Let's simplify. Imagine three partners: A, B, and C. Partner A purchases goods. The purchase binds A, B, and C because A acted on behalf of the firm. That is Mutual Agency. Every partner represents the business.

title: Real-Life Example: Mutual Agency

problem.en: Three doctors start a hospital. One doctor purchases MRI equipment. Are all three responsible?

steps.text: All three partners become responsible for that purchase.
Even if two partners were absent.

final_answer: Yes. Because each partner acts for the business as an agent.

title: Common Misconceptions
en:
❌ Partnership always means equal investment.
Correct: Investment can differ.

❌ Partnership means equal profit.
Correct: Profit sharing depends on agreement.

❌ Partnership must always have written agreement.
Correct: Many countries legally recognise oral agreements.

❌ Every partner must work.
Correct: Some partners invest only money.

title: Advantages & Limitations
en:
Advantages: More Capital, More Skills, Better Decisions, Risk Sharing, Specialisation, Business Growth.

Limitations: Unlimited Liability (in general partnerships), Possibility of Disputes, Profit Sharing, Mutual Trust Required, Business Continuity Challenges.

title: Accounting Importance & Effect
en:
Without Partnership, there is no Capital Account, Current Account, Profit Sharing Ratio, Interest on Capital, Interest on Drawings, Partner Salary, Partner Commission, Goodwill Adjustment, Admission, Retirement, Death of Partner.

Accounting Effect: Formation of Partnership creates Capital Accounts, Profit Sharing Agreement, Business Entity, and Separate Financial Records.

en: Yes, provided legal requirements are satisfied
Only if they have a written deed
Only if it is a registered firm

question.en: Can a minor become a partner?

en: Only admitted to the benefits of partnership under certain conditions

title: Think Beyond the Textbook
en: Imagine you are starting Shine Academy Naroda with one friend. What five conditions would you write in your Partnership Agreement before starting? Think about: Investment, Responsibilities, Decision making, Profit sharing, Exit of a partner.
